The hub has n - 1 neighbors and every rim node has three." width="100%"} Creates a hub node joined to every node of a cycle of `n - 1` rim nodes. The result has `n` nodes and `2(n - 1)` edges: `n - 1` spokes plus `n - 1` rim edges. The hub has degree `n - 1` and every rim node degree `3`. A wheel is a star whose spokes are joined into a ring, or equivalently a cycle with one extra node connected to everything. The hub is created first and the rim nodes follow it in order around the cycle. In a directed graph the spokes point outward from the hub and the rim runs in one direction (each rim node to the next, the last back to the first). The wheel is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Wheel graphs are useful for: - modeling a central coordinator plus a ring of peers that also talk to their neighbors (a hub-and-ring network) - test cases for centrality, where the hub dominates but rim nodes are not leaves - graph theory examples: wheels are planar, 3-connected, and self-dual, and `n=4` gives the complete graph `K4` ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes, counting the hub (so the rim has `n - 1` nodes). Must be at least `4`, so that the rim is at least a triangle. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; the hub gets the first number. A label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge (spokes and rim alike). If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `4`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A wheel with six nodes has a hub and a five-node rim, for `5` spokes plus `5` rim edges: ::: {#6e361ae1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_wheel_graph(n=6) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (6, 10) ``` ::: ::: The hub (node `"1"`) touches every rim node, while each rim node has its two rim neighbors plus the hub: ::: {#af344889 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df()["degree"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [5, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3] ``` ::: ::: The smallest wheel, `n=4`, is the complete graph on four nodes: ::: {#929aaec7 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_wheel_graph(n=4).is_isomorphic(ec.Graph().add_full_graph(n=4)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
